quickAnswer: Eski Foça (Old Foça) is a slow-paced Aegean fishing town 75 km north of İzmir Adnan Menderes Airport, known for Phocaean ruins, stone houses, and protected monk-seal waters around the Siren Rocks. Travellers choose this Cittaslow harbour over busier Çeşme for quiet coves, wooden boat excursions, and waterfront meze dinners.

body.text: How far is Eski Foça from İzmir Airport?

Eski Foça sits 75 km north of İzmir Adnan Menderes Airport (ADB), taking roughly 1 hour 10 minutes by rental car or private transfer via the İzmir ring road and Menemen. Without a car, combining the İZBAN suburban train with ESHOT bus line 744 takes about 2 hours 35 minutes door to door.

According to [Rome2Rio transit routing](https://www.rome2rio.com/s/Izmir-Airport-ADB/Fo%C3%A7a), driving is the most practical option if you carry luggage or plan to visit inland olive-growing villages such as Kozbeyli. Public transit works smoothly for light packers: board the northbound İZBAN rail directly from the airport station to Hatundere, then transfer to ESHOT municipal bus 744, which runs roughly every 20 minutes into Eski Foça town centre.

body.text: What boat trips explore the Siren Rocks and quiet coves?

Daily wooden excursion boats depart Eski Foça's Küçükdeniz harbour around 10:00–10:30 AM, cruising past the volcanic Siren Rocks and anchoring at clear swimming bays around Orak, İncir, and Fener islands. Because the archipelago is a protected Mediterranean monk seal sanctuary, boats reduce speed and never land on the Siren Rocks themselves.

The dramatic wind-carved cliffs of the Siren Rocks (Siren Kayalıkları) are linked to Homer's Odyssey and shelter caves used by critically endangered Mediterranean monk seals (Monachus monachus). As noted in [Old Foça conservation guidelines](https://traveltourshop.com/blog/old-foca-historic-stone-houses-siren-rocks-guide), Orak Island and the surrounding rocks hold 1st Degree Natural Site protection, making landing, spearfishing, or swimming into sea caves strictly illegal. Most full-day shared boats include a grilled-fish lunch and four swim stops at sheltered bays such as Kosova and Hayırsız Island; hiring a smaller private wooden boat lets you start earlier and linger in quieter coves.

items: Confirm departure pier at Küçükdeniz harbour the evening before in July and August.
Pack reef-safe sunscreen, a windbreaker for the afternoon Aegean breeze, and cash for drinks.
Bring binoculars rather than expecting close-up wildlife photos; monk seal sightings are rare and distant.
Ask the captain whether the itinerary includes İncir Island or outer coves if winds pick up.

body.text: Why is Foça preferred over busier Çeşme by slow travellers?

Foça appeals to slow travellers because strict archaeological and urban conservation rules prevent high-rise resorts and loud beach clubs from overtaking its stone-house peninsula. As an official member of the [Cittaslow International network](https://www.cittaslow.org/citta-slow/fo%C3%A7a), the town preserves small-scale fishing, weekly village markets, and walkable harbourfront lanes rather than Alaçatı-style nightlife.

More than 300 local families still earn a living from the sea around Eski and Yeni Foça, supporting a working harbour where nets are mended beside 19th-century stone residences. History sits directly underfoot: ancient Phokaia, founded by Ionian seafarers who later established Marseille, left behind the Temple of Athena, the waterfront ramparts of Beşkapılar Castle (Five Gates), and the Persian Monument (Taş Ev) just outside town. Compared with Çeşme's heavy weekend traffic and premium beach-club minimum spends, a foca izmir guide centres on unhurried walks, local yoghurt from Bağarası cooperatives, and quiet evenings by the water.
Where are the best harbourfront fish restaurants?

The strongest harbourfront fish tables line Küçükdeniz and Aşıklar Caddesi, where daily catch is displayed on ice and priced by weight alongside cold Aegean olive-oil mezes. Long-standing local staples such as [Fokai Balık Restaurant](https://mesprestiges.com/en/izmir/places/fokai-balik) and [Foça Liman Restaurant](https://izmir.com/restaurants/foca-liman-restaurant) serve red mullet (barbun), sea bream, and stuffed squid directly beside the moored boats.

Order the way locals do: inspect the fish cabinet first, confirm the kilo price before grilling, and pair your catch with seasonal greens such as deniz börülcesi (samphire), grilled octopus, and fava. Reserve a front-row table by early afternoon on Fridays and Saturdays between May and October, when İzmir residents drive north for sunset rakı and fish.

faq.q: What is the difference between Eski Foça and Yeni Foça?
faq.a: Eski Foça (Old Foça) is the historic peninsula with Phocaean ruins, stone houses, and the main excursion-boat harbour. Yeni Foça sits 20 km northeast along a wider sandy bay with summer villas and a smaller marina.

faq.q: Can you actually see Mediterranean monk seals in Foça?
faq.a: Sightings happen occasionally near the outer islands, but monk seals are shy and nocturnal. Treat any glimpse from a respectful distance as a lucky bonus rather than a guaranteed wildlife stop.

faq.q: How many nights should you spend in Eski Foça?
faq.a: Two to three nights give you enough time for a full-day cove boat trip, an unhurried walk through Beşkapılar and Phokaia ruins, and a morning drive to Kozbeyli village for dibek coffee.

faq.q: Are the beaches right in Eski Foça town sandy?
faq.a: The inner town waterfront has small pebble stretches and wooden swimming decks. Clearer water and wider pebble-or-sand coves lie a short drive or dolmuş ride away along Mersinaki Bay and towards Yeni Foça.

faq.q: Is Eski Foça suitable without a rental car?
faq.a: Yes, if you plan to stay on the peninsula, walk to dinner, and join boat trips from Küçükdeniz. Renting a car helps mainly for inland villages and outer beaches.

faq.q: When is the best month to visit Foça?
faq.a: May, June, and September bring warm swimming water, steady sunshine, and calm harbour evenings without peak-August crowding or chilly winter winds.
